notes: All three documents (CTL policies guide, CTL home page, student recommendations PDF) were found by both coders, both set stance to delegates, and new_types was empty on both sides. No school or computing-layer policy found; course layer deferred. Main disagreements: (1) unit_stance, the most frequent: neutral vs encourage/restrict/permit/require for advice that conditions use (verify output, cite, explain), resolved by whether the sentence takes a position on AI use itself (verification and citation guidance neutral; 'not as a replacement', 'never rely solely' restrict; optional transcripts permit, not require). (2) Phase general vs during-work/course-start for principles and instructor-role sentences, resolved by whether the sentence governs work with AI (during-work) or only states a role or rationale (general). (3) Actor for facts and quoted examples (instructor vs all vs student), resolved by who is bound or does the thing: no addressee gives all, 'Students could...' gives student. (4) Policy-type splits: P06 vs P04 vs P02 for the 'base level policy' and 'use only with permission' tiers (P04 for delegation, P06 for the unless-permitted rule), P30 vs P32 for 'guide, verify and craft' (P32), P45 vs P24 for AI sources 'must be properly quoted and cited' (P24), P56 vs P09 for the syllabus template (P09), P02 vs P44 for incorporating AI as a teaching tool (P44), P09 vs P36 for updating the integrity policy (P09). (5) Modality may vs should vs must resolved by the source's own verb ('can' gives may, 'should be prepared' gives should, 'allowed ... if' gives may). (6) Crossed alignments in the CTL policies guide (adjacent sentences of the same example) were re-paired by anchor text. Two sentences containing two rules were split: the draft/final-paper sample on the CTL home page (allowance P35 and ban P35) and the detector sentence ('not a definitive measure' P39, 'starting point of a conversation' P57; B's second unit counted as only_B). Only-A units (15): 14 kept as real statements (tier labels 'Use only with prior permission', 'Use only with acknowledgement', 'Use is freely permitted...'; AI definition; labor concern; neurodiversity and concept-understanding uses; 'no one-size-fits-all policy'), 1 dropped ('Let's remember to prompt responsibly' in the student PDF, the lead-in of a sentence coded as its own unit). Only-B units (13) all kept (e.g. 'will be treated as plagiarism', quoted examples on prose and idea generation, AI for everyday drafting tasks, instructors' responsibility to teach AI literacy). Where a final code matched neither coder's why, the why was rewritten; normalized policies were used only where an anchor was a fragment. Final file has 120 units (48, 52, 20).
